elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty running to Company and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Clause (a) covers "any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)" in favour of "the Company and its affiliates".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause (a)(i): "an allegation that the Site or any software, deliverable or service provided by HDI infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right" — tracks the Site/software/deliverables/services HDI supplies under Sections 1.1-1.9.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Clause (a)(iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Confidential Information, Content or Site user information caused by HDI" — HDI-caused data breach, framed in the Agreement's own data terminology.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Clause (a)(iv): "HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Clause (c): "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Clause (c): "the indemnifying Party shall control the defense of the claim" — control expressly allocated to the indemnifying Party.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Clause (c): "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in that defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Clause (b): Company indemnifies only "to the extent arising out of the Content supplied by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law", with the express backstop "the Company shall have no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Clause (a)(i) gives an IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity for the Site, software, deliverables and services provided by HDI.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the condition does not apply because the inserted indemnity contains no modification carve-out, which is more favourable to us than the fallback tolerates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out was added, so the tolerated exclusion is simply absent and the position is better than the fallback floor.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Company-specification carve-out appears in clause (a)(i); its absence favours us.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted Section contains only defence/indemnity and procedure; there is no operative obligation on HDI to procure a licence for continued use of, modify, or replace the infringing Site/software.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund fallback remedy appears anywhere in the inserted language or elsewhere in Sections 9-10.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No cap of any kind is stated; the drafter deliberately omitted the 3x super-cap because the Agreement has no limitation of liability, so importing one would create a ceiling that does not exist today.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all ten elements appear in operative text — HDI defence and indemnity for the Company and affiliates, IP infringement of the Site/software/deliverables/services, HDI breach of law, HDI-caused unauthorised access or disclosure, HDI gross negligence or willful misconduct, plus notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a Company indemnity expressly confined to Company-supplied Content and Company breach of law with a 'no other indemnification obligation' backstop.

Fallback level is incomplete (procure/modify/replace, refund and the 3x super-cap are all absent), but that is immaterial: position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, and the drafter's reason for not importing the super-cap into an agreement with no liability cap is sound and correctly stated in the comment.

Minimality holds: Section 9 warranties (including the Globix carve-out in 9(b)) and Section 10 are untouched, nothing is duplicated, and no term outside the INDEMN checklist (no cap, no insurance, no IP warranty) was added. A concise insertion is minimal here because the clause was wholly missing.
Intent is preserved: the insertion sits after the warranty section as the redline guidance directs and does not contradict the fee, term, exclusivity, cross-promotion or confidentiality mechanics.

Drafting cleanup (not an element failure): the rendered heading reads only 'Indemnification.' with no section number, while the comment calls it Section 9A. Number the clause in the operative text and conform Section 10.7 so the indemnity survives — as rendered, 10.7 survives 'Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10', which arguably does not capture an unnumbered or '9A' section; either number it 9(c) or add it to the 10.7 list.

Optional tightening (not required): clause (b) gives HDI a Company duty to 'defend' as well as indemnify; if we want the narrowest Company obligation, delete 'defend and' so we owe indemnity only. Also confirm 'Content' is a defined term in the Agreement so clauses (a)(iii) and (b) key off a fixed definition.
